overall: Atlanta is warming briskly this morning, with temperatures jumping from 73.4°F at 09:00 to 80.6°F by 11:05 ET — a sharp +7.2°F rise in two hours — and the current heating velocity of +3.6°F/hr confirms active and ongoing warming. The dewpoint of 60.8°F is moderate (not oppressively humid), which typically allows afternoon temps to climb further before moisture drag becomes a limiting factor. The day is trending hotter than a casual morning read might suggest, with peak heating still 4–5 hours away.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance shows notable spread: GFS is running hot at 90.3°F, while ECMWF (84.7°F) and NBM (83.3°F) are already under pressure given we are at 80.6°F with continued strong warming — NBM in particular looks likely to verify low. The ensemble signals are discouraging about the high-end tail (top tiers both rated Tier 4/Avoid at low probabilities), suggesting the GFS aggressive ceiling is unlikely to materialize.
max_temp_prediction: With the current base of 80.6°F and roughly 4–5 hours of diurnal heating remaining, even a decelerated warming pace of ~1–1.5°F/hr through the afternoon puts the peak in the 85–87°F range, which aligns best with ECMWF and splits the distance toward the ensemble odd-model signal near 87–88°F. Confidence is moderate — the spread between GFS and the consensus introduces meaningful uncertainty, but the ensemble Tier 4 signals argue against chasing the GFS upper bound.
